title: Proving/Checking Correctness with Invariants and Cases
learningObjectives: Explain the topic and its assumptions.
Describe why it matters in solving programming problems.
Interpret a small example or trace.
Apply the idea to a new situation.

understand.concept: Correctness means a solution satisfies its specification over the stated input domain. Tests provide evidence but may not cover every input. Invariants describe conditions that remain true at selected points in an algorithm. Case analysis separates categories such as empty, single-item, ordinary, boundary, and invalid inputs.
understand.whyItMatters: Systematic checking reveals hidden assumptions and helps explain why a method works, not just why one example passed.
understand.analogy: A checklist at each step preserves required conditions; an invariant is a condition that should remain true as the algorithm progresses.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the concept; real behavior depends on input, constraints, and implementation details.

explain.narrative: Define the task and assumptions, choose a method, trace it on a small example, then check edge cases.
